commit_message:
[Flow] Fold chained tensor.slice ops (#24628)

This PR Adds a canonicalization pattern for `flow.tensor.slice` that
folds only when the producer of the slice source is also a
`flow.tensor.slice`.

**Example :**

%producer = flow.tensor.slice %src[producer_start for producer_length]
%consumer = flow.tensor.slice %producer[consumer_start for
consumer_length]

**Canonicalizes to :**

%consumer = flow.tensor.slice %src[producer_start + consumer_start ] for
consumer_length

---------

commit_message:
[Flow] Fold chained tensor.slice ops (#24628)

This PR Adds a canonicalization pattern for `flow.tensor.slice` that
folds only when the producer of the slice source is also a
`flow.tensor.slice`.

**Example :**

%producer = flow.tensor.slice %src[producer_start for producer_length]
%consumer = flow.tensor.slice %producer[consumer_start for
consumer_length]

**Canonicalizes to :**

%consumer = flow.tensor.slice %src[producer_start + consumer_start ] for
consumer_length

commit_message:
Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@9c51ed38f1e2 (#24662)

Adapted compiler/src/iree/compiler/Codegen/Common/FoldTensorExtractOp.td
to specify invariant argument to memref.load, required due to:
f9f52bbcbc55 [mlir][memref] Add invariant attribute to memref.load
(#206197)
    
Re-generating the CAPI export files was required due to:
9889e626983f [mlir-c] Add IRMapping C API bindings (#206146)

Setting the module's targget triple in ROCM target due to:
00a6186128d3 AMDGPU: Prefer getting the triple from the module over the
TargetMachine (#206055)

Finding the LLVM commits and adapting the IREE code has been assistend
by Claude Code. The changes have been reviewed manually.

Signed-off-by: Stefan Schuermans <schuermans@roofline.ai>
name: setup_metadata

commit_message:
[ROCM] Validate that target triple is set in module and test for it (#24663)

Since LLVM commit
00a6186128d3 AMDGPU: Prefer getting the triple from the module over the
TargetMachine (#206055) the target riple of the module has to be set.

There was a suggestion for a dedicated test in
https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/24662#discussion_r3512817954.

Add the check for the target triple to the ROCM module validation and
add a LIT test for it.

This change has been assisted by Claude Code. The changes have been
reviewed manually before opening the PR.

Signed-off-by: Stefan Schuermans <schuermans@roofline.ai>
name: Tag candidate release

commit_message:
Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@9c51ed38f1e2 (#24662)

Adapted compiler/src/iree/compiler/Codegen/Common/FoldTensorExtractOp.td
to specify invariant argument to memref.load, required due to:
f9f52bbcbc55 [mlir][memref] Add invariant attribute to memref.load
(#206197)
    
Re-generating the CAPI export files was required due to:
9889e626983f [mlir-c] Add IRMapping C API bindings (#206146)

Setting the module's targget triple in ROCM target due to:
00a6186128d3 AMDGPU: Prefer getting the triple from the module over the
TargetMachine (#206055)

Finding the LLVM commits and adapting the IREE code has been assistend
by Claude Code. The changes have been reviewed manually.

Signed-off-by: Stefan Schuermans <schuermans@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[Flow] Fold chained tensor.slice ops (#24628)

This PR Adds a canonicalization pattern for `flow.tensor.slice` that
folds only when the producer of the slice source is also a
`flow.tensor.slice`.

**Example :**

%producer = flow.tensor.slice %src[producer_start for producer_length]
%consumer = flow.tensor.slice %producer[consumer_start for
consumer_length]

**Canonicalizes to :**

%consumer = flow.tensor.slice %src[producer_start + consumer_start ] for
consumer_length

---------

Signed-off-by: LekkalaSravya3 <lekkala.sravya@multicorewareinc.com>

commit_message:
[Flow] Fold chained tensor.slice ops (#24628)

This PR Adds a canonicalization pattern for `flow.tensor.slice` that
folds only when the producer of the slice source is also a
`flow.tensor.slice`.

**Example :**

%producer = flow.tensor.slice %src[producer_start for producer_length]
%consumer = flow.tensor.slice %producer[consumer_start for
consumer_length]

**Canonicalizes to :**

%consumer = flow.tensor.slice %src[producer_start + consumer_start ] for
consumer_length

---------

Signed-off-by: LekkalaSravya3 <lekkala.sravya@multicorewareinc.com>

commit_message:
Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@9c51ed38f1e2 (#24662)

Adapted compiler/src/iree/compiler/Codegen/Common/FoldTensorExtractOp.td
to specify invariant argument to memref.load, required due to:
f9f52bbcbc55 [mlir][memref] Add invariant attribute to memref.load
(#206197)
    
Re-generating the CAPI export files was required due to:
9889e626983f [mlir-c] Add IRMapping C API bindings (#206146)

Setting the module's targget triple in ROCM target due to:
00a6186128d3 AMDGPU: Prefer getting the triple from the module over the
TargetMachine (#206055)

Finding the LLVM commits and adapting the IREE code has been assistend
by Claude Code. The changes have been reviewed manually.

Signed-off-by: Stefan Schuermans <schuermans@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[GlobalOpt] Add pass to convert broadcast batch_matmul to matmul

Add `iree-global-opt-convert-broadcast-batch-matmul-to-matmul`, which
rewrites a `linalg.batch_matmul` whose RHS is a weight broadcast on the
batch dimension into `tensor.collapse_shape` + `linalg.matmul` +
`tensor.expand_shape`:

  broadcast(weight) + batch_matmul  ->  collapse(act) + matmul + expand

The broadcast is recognized both as a `linalg.broadcast` and as the
generalized `linalg.generic` form produced by GeneralizeLinalgNamedOps.
Both plain and transpose_b batch_matmul are handled.

Batched activations against a single shared weight (batched linear layers,
attention projections, ...) arrive as a batch_matmul whose RHS is a 2-D
weight broadcast across the batch. That materializes the broadcast and runs
a batched contraction for what is really a plain matmul. Collapsing the
batch into the M dimension yields a regular matmul, drops the broadcast and
lands on the better-tuned matmul / data-tiling path.

The pass runs before transpose propagation so the pure broadcast is matched
before it gets fused with a transpose into a generic.

transpose_a is intentionally not handled: collapsing the LHS
[batch, K, M] -> [batch*K, M] and the output [batch, M, N] -> [batch*M, N]
do not agree, so the rewrite would be incorrect. Negative tests cover this,
plus a broadcast on the LHS, a broadcast on a non-batch dimension, and a
fused broadcast+transpose generic.

Co-authored-by: ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>
Signed-off-by: Roberto Laudani <laudani@roofline.ai>

Add `iree-global-opt-convert-broadcast-batch-matmul-to-matmul`, which
rewrites a `linalg.batch_matmul` whose RHS is a weight broadcast on the
batch dimension into `tensor.collapse_shape` + `linalg.matmul` +
`tensor.expand_shape`:

  broadcast(weight) + batch_matmul  ->  collapse(act) + matmul + expand

The broadcast is recognized both as a `linalg.broadcast` and as the
generalized `linalg.generic` form produced by GeneralizeLinalgNamedOps.
Both plain and transpose_b batch_matmul are handled.

Batched activations against a single shared weight (batched linear layers,
attention projections, ...) arrive as a batch_matmul whose RHS is a 2-D
weight broadcast across the batch. That materializes the broadcast and runs
a batched contraction for what is really a plain matmul. Collapsing the
batch into the M dimension yields a regular matmul, drops the broadcast and
lands on the better-tuned matmul / data-tiling path.

The pass runs before transpose propagation so the pure broadcast is matched
before it gets fused with a transpose into a generic.

transpose_a is intentionally not handled: collapsing the LHS
[batch, K, M] -> [batch*K, M] and the output [batch, M, N] -> [batch*M, N]
do not agree, so the rewrite would be incorrect. Negative tests cover this,
plus a broadcast on the LHS, a broadcast on a non-batch dimension, and a
fused broadcast+transpose generic.

Co-authored-by: ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>
Signed-off-by: Roberto Laudani <laudani@roofline.ai>
name: runtime :: macos-14

Add `iree-global-opt-convert-broadcast-batch-matmul-to-matmul`, which
rewrites a `linalg.batch_matmul` whose RHS is a weight broadcast on the
batch dimension into `tensor.collapse_shape` + `linalg.matmul` +
`tensor.expand_shape`:

  broadcast(weight) + batch_matmul  ->  collapse(act) + matmul + expand

The broadcast is recognized both as a `linalg.broadcast` and as the
generalized `linalg.generic` form produced by GeneralizeLinalgNamedOps.
Both plain and transpose_b batch_matmul are handled.

Batched activations against a single shared weight (batched linear layers,
attention projections, ...) arrive as a batch_matmul whose RHS is a 2-D
weight broadcast across the batch. That materializes the broadcast and runs
a batched contraction for what is really a plain matmul. Collapsing the
batch into the M dimension yields a regular matmul, drops the broadcast and
lands on the better-tuned matmul / data-tiling path.

The pass runs before transpose propagation so the pure broadcast is matched
before it gets fused with a transpose into a generic.

transpose_a is intentionally not handled: collapsing the LHS
[batch, K, M] -> [batch*K, M] and the output [batch, M, N] -> [batch*M, N]
do not agree, so the rewrite would be incorrect. Negative tests cover this,
plus a broadcast on the LHS, a broadcast on a non-batch dimension, and a
fused broadcast+transpose generic.

Co-authored-by: ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>
Signed-off-by: Roberto Laudani <laudani@roofline.ai>
name: runtime_tracing :: ubuntu-24.04 :: tracy

commit_message:
[GlobalOpt] Add pass to convert broadcast batch_matmul to matmul

Add `iree-global-opt-convert-broadcast-batch-matmul-to-matmul`, which
rewrites a `linalg.batch_matmul` whose RHS is a weight broadcast on the
batch dimension into `tensor.collapse_shape` + `linalg.matmul` +
`tensor.expand_shape`:

  broadcast(weight) + batch_matmul  ->  collapse(act) + matmul + expand

The broadcast is recognized both as a `linalg.broadcast` and as the
generalized `linalg.generic` form produced by GeneralizeLinalgNamedOps.
Both plain and transpose_b batch_matmul are handled.

Batched activations against a single shared weight (batched linear layers,
attention projections, ...) arrive as a batch_matmul whose RHS is a 2-D
weight broadcast across the batch. That materializes the broadcast and runs
a batched contraction for what is really a plain matmul. Collapsing the
batch into the M dimension yields a regular matmul, drops the broadcast and
lands on the better-tuned matmul / data-tiling path.

The pass runs before transpose propagation so the pure broadcast is matched
before it gets fused with a transpose into a generic.

transpose_a is intentionally not handled: collapsing the LHS
[batch, K, M] -> [batch*K, M] and the output [batch, M, N] -> [batch*M, N]
do not agree, so the rewrite would be incorrect. Negative tests cover this,
plus a broadcast on the LHS, a broadcast on a non-batch dimension, and a
fused broadcast+transpose generic.

commit_message:
[Codegen][CPU] Fill in the bf16 and i8 ukernel bodies + e2e tests. (#24572)

Replaces the bf16 and i8-VNNI seeds' stub bodies with real SIMD
implementations, both generic over the `intrinsics_{m,n,k}` unrolling
factors and structured like the AMDGPU C ukernel they were adapted from
(`iree_uk_amdgpu_multi_mma_mfma_i32_16x16x32_i8`): accumulators in
registers, an outer loop over the K tiles (`k_outer`), and inside it the
`(intrinsics_m, intrinsics_n, intrinsics_k)` unroll. The `intrinsics_*`
arrive as constants at the inlined call site, so the loops fully unroll
and the `acc_regs` arrays become fixed register files -- the bitcode-LTO
equivalent of a C++ template, as the README describes.

- bf16 (`MMA_X86_AVX512BF16_1x16x2_F32_BF16`): one `_mm512_dpbf16_ps`
per (m, n, k), with the LHS K-pair broadcast via `set1_ps`.
- i8 (`MMA_X86_AVX512VNNI_16x16x2_I32_I8_CASTI16`): the 16x16x2 tile is
bit-compatible with the codegen path `lowerX86Avx512Vnni16x16x2I8` --
one `vpmovsxbw` widen of each i8 panel to i16, the `vpshufd` /
`vbroadcasti32x4` fan-out, and 16 `vpdpwssd` over the block-interleaved
(rlo, chi, rhi, clo) ACC layout. The i8 ukernel needs `-mavx512bw` for
the widen, so it is added to the VNNI copts.

`LLVMCPUSelectUKernels` now only selects a ukernel when its bitcode
actually exists (via `attachUKernelBitcodeOnOp`'s bool return), so an
`MMAIntrinsic` the cost model picks but for which no seed exists -- e.g.
the M<->N-swapped `MMA_X86_AVX512BF16_16x1x2_F32_BF16` -- falls back to
codegen instead of dangling an undefined symbol.

Adds two execution/numerical tests, the first of the new C-bitcode
ukernel path: `e2e_matmul_cpu_dt_inner_tiled_llvm_ukernel_bf16_f32`
(avx512bf16) and `..._i8_i32` (avx512vnni). Each compiles a data-tiled
matmul with `--iree-llvmcpu-enable-llvm-ukernels=inner_tiled`, links the
ukernel bitcode, runs on host and checks results against a reference --
exercising the operand threading and generic `intrinsics_{m,n,k}`
unrolling that the IR-level lit tests cannot. Both were confirmed to
actually select their ukernel (not silently fall back to codegen).

Progress towards https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/24574.

arrive as constants at the inlined call site, so the loops fully unroll
and the `acc_regs` arrays become fixed register files -- the bitcode-LTO

(avx512bf16) and `..._i8_i32` (avx512vnni). Each compiles a data-tiled
matmul with `--iree-llvmcpu-enable-llvm-ukernels=inner_tiled`, links the
ukernel bitcode, runs on host and checks results against a reference --
exercising the operand threading and generic `intrinsics_{m,n,k}`
unrolling that the IR-level lit tests cannot. Both were confirmed to
actually select their ukernel (not silently fall back to codegen).

Progress towards https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/24574.

commit_message:
[Codegen][CPU] Add design doc for the LLVMCPU C-ukernel framework.

Adds README.md for compiler/plugins/target/LLVMCPU/builtins/ukernel/ as a
single final documentation commit, rather than iterating the doc across
the earlier framework commits (less churn for review).

Covers: scope (the framework is op-agnostic in principle, with
`inner_tiled` as the initial and primary case getting the detailed
treatment — inner-K-loop-only contract, and how specialization splits
between symbol selection on the `MMAIntrinsic` and post-inlining loop
unrolling on the `intrinsics_{m,n,k}` factors); the two structural
pillars (lives in compiler/, bitcode-only; self-contained IR via
`hal.executable_object`); the end-to-end lowering flow; the
`--iree-llvmcpu-enable-llvm-ukernels` user flag; bring-your-own-ukernel;
an authoring guide; testing at both the lit (compiler IR) and
`tests/e2e/matmul` (numerical) levels; and the three seed examples.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Benoit Jacob <jacob.benoit.1@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[Codegen][CPU] Fill in the bf16 and i8 ukernel bodies + e2e tests.

Replaces the bf16 and i8-VNNI seeds' stub bodies with real SIMD
implementations, both generic over the `intrinsics_{m,n,k}` unrolling
factors and structured like the AMDGPU C ukernel they were adapted from
(`iree_uk_amdgpu_multi_mma_mfma_i32_16x16x32_i8`): accumulators in
registers, an outer loop over the K tiles (`k_outer`), and inside it the
`(intrinsics_m, intrinsics_n, intrinsics_k)` unroll. The `intrinsics_*`
arrive as constants at the inlined call site, so the loops fully unroll
and the `acc_regs` arrays become fixed register files -- the bitcode-LTO
equivalent of a C++ template, as the README describes.

  - bf16 (`MMA_X86_AVX512BF16_1x16x2_F32_BF16`): one `_mm512_dpbf16_ps`
    per (m, n, k), with the LHS K-pair broadcast via `set1_ps`.
  - i8 (`MMA_X86_AVX512VNNI_16x16x2_I32_I8_CASTI16`): the 16x16x2 tile is
    bit-compatible with the codegen path `lowerX86Avx512Vnni16x16x2I8` --
    one `vpmovsxbw` widen of each i8 panel to i16, the `vpshufd` /
    `vbroadcasti32x4` fan-out, and 16 `vpdpwssd` over the block-interleaved
    (rlo, chi, rhi, clo) ACC layout. The i8 ukernel needs `-mavx512bw` for
    the widen, so it is added to the VNNI copts.

`LLVMCPUSelectUKernels` now only selects a ukernel when its bitcode
actually exists (via `attachUKernelBitcodeOnOp`'s bool return), so an
`MMAIntrinsic` the cost model picks but for which no seed exists -- e.g.
the M<->N-swapped `MMA_X86_AVX512BF16_16x1x2_F32_BF16` -- falls back to
codegen instead of dangling an undefined symbol.

Adds two execution/numerical tests, the first of the new C-bitcode
ukernel path: `e2e_matmul_cpu_dt_inner_tiled_llvm_ukernel_bf16_f32`
(avx512bf16) and `..._i8_i32` (avx512vnni). Each compiles a data-tiled
matmul with `--iree-llvmcpu-enable-llvm-ukernels=inner_tiled`, links the
ukernel bitcode, runs on host and checks results against a reference --
exercising the operand threading and generic `intrinsics_{m,n,k}`
unrolling that the IR-level lit tests cannot. Both were confirmed to
actually select their ukernel (not silently fall back to codegen).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Benoit Jacob <jacob.benoit.1@gmail.com>

implementations, both generic over the `intrinsics_{m,n,k}` unrolling
factors and structured like the AMDGPU C ukernel they were adapted from
(`iree_uk_amdgpu_multi_mma_mfma_i32_16x16x32_i8`): accumulators in
registers, an outer loop over the K tiles (`k_outer`), and inside it the
`(intrinsics_m, intrinsics_n, intrinsics_k)` unroll. The `intrinsics_*`
arrive as constants at the inlined call site, so the loops fully unroll
and the `acc_regs` arrays become fixed register files -- the bitcode-LTO
equivalent of a C++ template, as the README describes.

  - bf16 (`MMA_X86_AVX512BF16_1x16x2_F32_BF16`): one `_mm512_dpbf16_ps`
    per (m, n, k), with the LHS K-pair broadcast via `set1_ps`.

commit_message:
[Flow] Fold chained tensor.slice ops (#24628)

This PR Adds a canonicalization pattern for `flow.tensor.slice` that
folds only when the producer of the slice source is also a
`flow.tensor.slice`.

**Example :**

%producer = flow.tensor.slice %src[producer_start for producer_length]
%consumer = flow.tensor.slice %producer[consumer_start for
consumer_length]

**Canonicalizes to :**

%consumer = flow.tensor.slice %src[producer_start + consumer_start ] for
consumer_length

---------

commit_message:
[InputConversion][TOSA]: change TOSA level to none

For some TOSA lowering use-cases, we will have dynamic batch sizes
and this will trigger the level check. Here we set the level to none
so that dynamic dimensions are allowed in TOSA IR.

The TOSA level check ensures that tensor sizes are within a certain
threshold but for our use-case with TFlite this is not always the case.

commit_message:
[Flow] Fold chained tensor.slice ops (#24628)

This PR Adds a canonicalization pattern for `flow.tensor.slice` that
folds only when the producer of the slice source is also a
`flow.tensor.slice`.

**Example :**

%producer = flow.tensor.slice %src[producer_start for producer_length]
%consumer = flow.tensor.slice %producer[consumer_start for
consumer_length]

**Canonicalizes to :**

%consumer = flow.tensor.slice %src[producer_start + consumer_start ] for
consumer_length

---------

Signed-off-by: LekkalaSravya3 <lekkala.sravya@multicorewareinc.com>
name: macos_x64_clang

commit_message:
[GlobalOpt] Add pass to convert broadcast batch_matmul to matmul

Add `iree-global-opt-convert-broadcast-batch-matmul-to-matmul`, which
rewrites a `linalg.batch_matmul` whose RHS is a weight broadcast on the
batch dimension into `tensor.collapse_shape` + `linalg.matmul` +
`tensor.expand_shape`:

  broadcast(weight) + batch_matmul  ->  collapse(act) + matmul + expand

The broadcast is recognized both as a `linalg.broadcast` and as the
generalized `linalg.generic` form produced by GeneralizeLinalgNamedOps.
Both plain and transpose_b batch_matmul are handled.

Batched activations against a single shared weight (batched linear layers,
attention projections, ...) arrive as a batch_matmul whose RHS is a 2-D
weight broadcast across the batch. That materializes the broadcast and runs
a batched contraction for what is really a plain matmul. Collapsing the
batch into the M dimension yields a regular matmul, drops the broadcast and
lands on the better-tuned matmul / data-tiling path.

The pass runs before transpose propagation so the pure broadcast is matched
before it gets fused with a transpose into a generic.

transpose_a is intentionally not handled: collapsing the LHS
[batch, K, M] -> [batch*K, M] and the output [batch, M, N] -> [batch*M, N]
do not agree, so the rewrite would be incorrect. Negative tests cover this,
plus a broadcast on the LHS, a broadcast on a non-batch dimension, and a
fused broadcast+transpose generic.

Co-authored-by: ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>
Signed-off-by: Roberto Laudani <laudani@roofline.ai>
